newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's rating of HK unit CDs unfair-Bank of China. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Moody's rating of HK unit CDs unfair-Bank of China. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]

text.p: The Bank of China on Monday blasted Moody's Investors Service for rating the recent floating rate certificate of deposit issue of the bank's Hong Kong branch at Baa1.
"We are of the opinion that Moody's ratings are unfair and not objective," the bank said in a release.
Bank of China said its Hong Kong branch is subject "to the strict supervision of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority."

The bank said its Hong Kong branch has a sound business, a solid capital base and strong creditability. It said the branch's financial strength is comparable to other banks of similar size in the territory.
"Since Moody's ratings do not reflect the actual position of the Bank of China, Hong Kong branch, they are received with much regret," Bank of China said.
Bank of China went on to say that Moody's view of the bank is not shared by the market, which responded enthusiastically to the its latest FRCD.

"According to our preliminary counting, there are more than 60 financial institutions who have committed a total participation amount of over HK$9 billion, 4.5 times our issued amount," Bank of China said.
The five-year FRCD (corrects tenor) pays a margin of 35 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an all-in return of 41.5 basis points to top-tier participants.

The Bank of China Hong Kong branch suspended a HK$5 billion FRCD last year after Moody's downgrade of its rating to Baa1 made the issue ineligible for the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF), or discount window.
Eligibility for LAF makes an issue more attractive to banks because holders of the qualifying debt can engage in repurchase agreements with the monetary authority, increasing liquidity.
But earlier this year, the HKMA said it would accept ratings from Japan Bond Research Institute (JBRI) and IBCA in addition to Moody's and Standard and Poor's Corp when considering LAF eligibility.
Bank of China said the latest FRCD has been given a preliminary rating of AA-minus from the JBRI, which would make it eligible for LAF.
